fixtures.synthetic_description: Derived from a saved stone stack by adding tag.x as an empty Byte list or empty Compound list. Native parsing, reconstruction and copied-item save preserved both declared types.

results.operations: Constructed native ItemStack from native parsed saved NBT, copied to public SDK ItemStack, destroyed native temporary and parsed source tag. Made a second public SDK copy. Added an Int marker to the first copy user metadata through getNbt/setNbt. Compared its native save after public conversion and removal of the marker against original saved bytes. The untouched sibling remained byte-identical. Changed the edited copy amount to1 (a supported value) and destroyed it; the sibling save still matched.
results.count_limit: Amount1 is unchanged for unstackable fixtures; multi-count fixtures changed. Endstone rejects setAmount0. That invalid call was found in preflight before diagnostic execution and was replaced; this run makes no zero-count clearing claim.
results.metadata_limit: The two typed-empty-list items also failed the baseline native-to-public NBT comparison before editing. Public conversion cannot retain their declared element types. The complete public getNbt/setNbt/conversion path therefore remains unsuitable for unrestricted metadata-preserving writeback. All64 items passed the direct native parser/save comparisons.
results.repeatability: Both64-row result sets were identical. Fixture files remained unchanged and all diagnostic objects were detached from player inventories.

limitations: Private diagnostic only; no public reconstruction/write operation exported
No live inventory reassignment or authoritative dynamic-container mapping
No held UI or editor submission
No durable identity, save barrier, crash injection or recovery qualification
No claim of safe arbitrary public-NBT edits
No Windows inference; raw NBT and worlds remain private
